chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Dawood al-Raqqi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And there is not a single thing but it Glorifies Him with His praise, but you do not understand their Glorification.' He said: 'The cracking of the wall is its Glorification.'
ai.seo_question: What does the Quran mean when it says things glorify God but we do not understand their glorification?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), the concept of universal glorification (tasbih) is expanded beyond linguistic praise to include the physical state of all entities, illustrated by the cracking of walls as a form of submission to God's will. This aligns with the Shia exegetical tradition that views the entire cosmos as actively worshipping its Creator, even if humans lack the capacity to comprehend the specific modes of this worship. It underscores the metaphysical reality that every atom and structure in existence is engaged in a continuous act of divine praise.
